title: Scaffold Rust project: workspace, deps, error handling, CI skeleton
description: Create the Cargo project layout for the Rust aterm. Module skeleton mirroring the planned layers (recorder, asciicast, ashirt/network, config, tui, update). Add core deps and error-handling conventions (anyhow at boundaries, thiserror for typed errors). Add a minimal CI skeleton (build + clippy + fmt) that later issues extend. Avoid serde_yaml/serde_yml (deprecated/unsound) -- standardize on serde_yaml_ng; remember reqwest 0.13 needs the multipart feature when added.
acceptance_criteria: cargo build, cargo clippy, and cargo fmt --check pass; module skeleton compiles; CI workflow runs build+clippy+fmt.

title: Rewrite aterm in Rust on asciicast v3 (Option B)
description: Port aterm (Go terminal-recording + ASHIRT evidence client) to Rust. asciinema 3.x is GPL binary-only with no library, so we do NOT depend on it; we reimplement the asciicast v3 format ourselves (permissive, keeps aterm MIT) and rebuild the ASHIRT layers on well-supported Rust crates. asciinema/avt (Apache-2.0) is reference + optional playback only. Target Linux/macOS, plus Windows via portable-pty/ConPTY + crossterm. ALL work branches off the rust-rewrite integration branch, never main; merge to main only after verification.

title: Application entry point and orchestration
description: Wire everything together (replaces Go cmd/aterm/climain.go). Flow: parse CLI -> load layered config -> first-run if config missing or --reset/-hard -> set base URL/keys -> validate (show menu on failure) -> update notification -> init recording -> start in recording or main-menu view per flags. Handle -pc (print config), version flags, -m/--menu.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end: fresh run triggers first-run; configured run records and offers upload; flags (-m, -pc, --reset, version) behave as documented; matches the Go climain control flow.

title: Main menu + recording flow
description: Port the main menu and recording entry flow (replaces Go appdialogs/main_menu.go + recording start). Operation selection (from the ops API), start-recording action that runs the recorder writing to outputDir/slug/name, and surrounding menu navigation. Uses the TUI foundation. Keep recording and menu as distinct phases.
acceptance_criteria: From the menu a user can pick an operation and record a session to the correct path; menu navigation (select/search) works; returns to menu after recording.

title: ASHIRT HTTP client base
description: Build the reqwest-based client (replaces Go network/common.go plumbing). Base URL handling (append /api), JSON request helper, response body parsing, status-code error mapping (401 -> auth error, 500 -> server error, etc.), and attaching the HMAC Authorization + Date headers to every request. Use the blocking client (simplest given the menu-driven flow) and document the choice.
acceptance_criteria: Against a mock HTTP server a signed GET/POST round-trips; auth headers present and correctly formed; status-code error mapping unit-tested.

title: PTY recording core
description: Implement terminal recording (replaces Go cmd/aterm/recording/* + eventers/ + recorders/). Spawn a subshell in a PTY via portable-pty (ConPTY on Windows), put the controlling terminal in raw mode (crossterm), tee child output to both the user terminal and the event pipeline, forward user input to the child, and handle resize (SIGWINCH on unix / ConPTY resize on Windows) updating term size. Feed output bytes as timestamped o events to the v3 writer; emit a final x exit-status event. Avoid the Go copyRouter stdin-routing hack -- keep record and menu as separate phases.
acceptance_criteria: Records a real shell session to a .cast that plays correctly in asciinema play; resize reflected via r events; raw mode restored on exit even on error; exit status captured.

title: TUI foundation: prompt/menu primitives
description: Establish the interactive UI layer (replaces Go promptui + dialog/ + fancy/). Use inquire (Select/MultiSelect/Confirm/Text/Password with filtering) on a crossterm backend, plus shared styling helpers. Provide reusable wrappers: searchable select list, yes/no, text prompt, multiselect. crossterm also provides raw-mode and resize-event handling reused by the recorder.
acceptance_criteria: A demo exercises searchable select, multiselect, confirm, and text prompts; builds and runs on Linux; styling helpers unit-tested where practical.

title: Config model + layered loading
description: Port aterm config (replaces Go cmd/aterm/config/config.go). Layered precedence: defaults < YAML file < env (ASHIRT_TERM_RECORDER_*) < CLI flags. Fields: configVersion, apiURL, outputDir, accessKey, secretKey, outputFileName, operationSlug, recordingShell. YAML via serde_yaml_ng. Config path via the directories crate (XDG on unix, LOCALAPPDATA on Windows): config/aterm/config.yaml. CLI via clap v4 derive. Implement read, write, and pretty-print.
acceptance_criteria: Tests verify precedence (file < env < CLI), round-trip read/write, and correct paths on unix; clap parses the documented flags (-s/--shell, --operation, -m/--menu, --reset, --reset-hard, -pc, version).

title: ASHIRT HMAC request signing
description: Port ashirt-server/signer (replaces Go network/common.go auth). Authorization = accessKey + ':' + base64(HMAC-SHA256(key, canonical)) where canonical = METHOD + LF + REQUEST_URI(including query) + LF + Date(RFC1123 GMT) + LF + sha256(body). Use hmac 0.13 + sha2 0.11 (pin compatible majors). GET uses empty body. This MUST match the server byte-for-byte -- the top integration risk.
acceptance_criteria: Unit test reproduces a known-good signature fixture (mirror the Go signer vectors); Date header is RFC1123 in GMT; query string included in the signed URI.

title: asciicast v3 writer + types
description: Implement the asciicast v3 format writer (replaces Go formatters/asciicast_*). NDJSON: line 1 header, then event lines. Header: version 3, term:{cols,rows}, optional term.type and term.theme, timestamp, env, title, tags. Events: [interval, code, data] where interval is seconds since the PREVIOUS event (relative timing -- the key v3 change from v2); codes o/i/r/x (x = exit status). Allow comment lines starting with #. Provide a streaming writer that takes timestamped events and computes intervals.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover header + event serialization and interval computation; a sample file validates against the asciicast v3 spec and plays in asciinema play.

title: Cross-platform CI + release binaries
description: Extend CI to build/test on Linux, macOS, and Windows and produce release binaries for each (replaces the Go release workflow). Verify the Windows ConPTY recording path actually works (asciinema upstream does NOT support Windows, so this path is ours to validate). Upload release artifacts on tags.
acceptance_criteria: CI green on all three OSes; release workflow produces downloadable binaries; a Windows-recorded .cast opens in a player.

title: Post-recording upload menu
description: Port the post-record menu (replaces Go appdialogs/upload_menu.go). After a recording: Upload (collect description, multiselect tags with create-new-tag option, submit via upload API), Rename recording file, Discard recording, Return to main menu. Uses tags API + upload API + TUI foundation.
acceptance_criteria: After a recording the menu offers upload/rename/discard/return; upload collects description + tags and submits; rename and discard manipulate the file correctly.

title: Config validation + first-run wizard + ASHIRT import
description: Port validation + first-run (replaces Go config validation + appdialogs/first_run_prompt.go). Validate: accessKey set, secretKey set and base64-decodable (reuse signing decode), apiURL parseable. First-run interactive wizard (inquire) collecting API URL / access key / secret key / output dir, able to seed defaults from the ASHIRT desktop app config (config/ashirt/config.json). Support --reset (seed from existing) and --reset-hard (ignore existing).
acceptance_criteria: Validation returns aggregated errors for missing/invalid fields; first-run writes a valid config; ASHIRT config.json values imported when present; --reset vs --reset-hard behave as documented.

title: ASHIRT operations + tags API
description: Port operations/tags endpoints (replaces Go network/get_operations.go + tagging.go). GET /operations, GET /operations/{slug}/tags, POST /operations/{slug}/tags (create tag with name + colorName; random color helper). Typed Operation and Tag structs.
acceptance_criteria: Against a mock server: list operations, list tags, and create tag work and deserialize; random color helper returns a valid palette color.

title: ASHIRT evidence multipart upload
description: Port evidence upload (replaces Go network/upload.go). multipart/form-data POST to /operations/{slug}/evidence with fields notes, contentType (terminal-recording), tagIds (JSON array) and the .cast file part. reqwest with features=[multipart] (+ blocking). Parse the created-evidence response; map non-201 to a useful error using the server error field.
acceptance_criteria: Against a mock server, uploads a file with correct fields and content type; 201 parsed; non-201 surfaces the server error message.

title: GitHub release update check
description: Port the update check (replaces Go network/github.go). Query the repo GitHub releases (octocrab), parse loose semver tags (optional leading v; major/minor/patch + extra), and report available major/minor/patch upgrades vs the current version. Optionally wire self_update for in-place binary replacement (Go aterm only notifies).
acceptance_criteria: Semver parse/compare unit tests match Go behavior (ignore extra in comparisons); given a mocked releases list, correctly classifies major/minor/patch upgrades.

title: (Optional) Playback / preview via avt
description: Optional, post-MVP. Add playback/preview using the avt crate (Apache-2.0 VT emulator) -- local replay and/or generating a snapshot/thumbnail of an evidence recording. Purely additive; not required for parity with Go aterm.
acceptance_criteria: Can replay a recorded .cast locally and/or render a final-frame snapshot; gated behind a feature/subcommand so it does not affect the core path.
